title: Private Deployments: Backup/Restore Dashboards + Alerting (Mock v0.3)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Private Deployments: Backup/Restore Dashboards + Alerting (Mock v0.3)
- Audience: Private customers (ops teams), Redwood SRE/on-call, Solutions
- Scope: control-plane backups + scheduled restore drills (staging + optionally customer prod)
- Non-goal: full K8s cluster DR visualization (etcd restore has separate runbook/dashboard)

Speaker notes:
This is a mock that matches how we expect metrics to look once the backup/restore toolkit is shipping broadly. The goal is a single “DR readiness” view that answers: are backups happening, are they usable, and can we restore within RTO.

—

Slide 2 — What questions the dashboard must answer
1) Are backups running on schedule?
- Last successful backup per deployment
- Success rate over time
- Failure causes + whether action is needed

2) Are backups usable?
- Integrity verification results (manifest + checksums)
- Artifact size trend (early signal for runaway growth)

3) Can we restore within target RTO?
- Restore drill success/failure
- Restore drill duration (end-to-end)
- Validation outcomes (post-restore smoke tests)

4) Are we paging correctly (not noisy)?
- Alert gating during maintenance windows
- Separate policies for staging drills vs prod backups

Speaker notes:
We’ve had failures where a backup “succeeds” but restore fails due to ordering / missing CRDs / permissions. So we need both “backup succeeded” and “restore drill works” as separate signals.

—

Slide 3 — Data model / labeling conventions (for filters)
Proposed common labels across metrics and logs:
- deployment_id: <customer-or-internal-deployment-uuid>
- deployment_type: vpc | onprem | airgapped
- env: prod | staging | dev
- region: us-east-1 | eu-west-1 | onprem
- cluster_id: <k8s cluster>
- backup_scope: control_plane | k8s_manifests | audit_logs
- storage_backend: s3 | nfs | gcs
- kms_provider: aws-kms | gcp-kms | hsm | local
- job_type: scheduled | ad_hoc | restore_drill

Speaker notes:
If we can’t filter by deployment_id + env cleanly, on-call triage becomes painful and we risk cross-tenant confusion. Also: “backup_scope” is important to avoid implying we back up things we don’t (e.g., model weights in a customer registry).

—

Slide 4 — Dashboard layout (top-level)
Dashboard name: “Private DR Readiness — Backup/Restore”
Sections:
A) Executive tiles (red/green)
- Backup freshness (prod)
- Backup success rate (7d)
- Restore drill success (30d)
- Restore drill p95 duration (30d)

B) Backup health (time series + tables)
- Success/fail counts
- Last success timestamp
- Duration + bytes
- Error categories and top failing deployments

C) Restore drill health
- Drill outcomes
- Duration breakdown
- Validation checklist results

D) Alert status + runbook shortcuts
- Active alerts (by severity)
- Links: backup runbook, restore runbook, DR plan templates

Speaker notes:
We want a “one scroll” experience with obvious “what’s broken” at top, and drill-down below.

—

Slide 5 — Mock: Executive tiles (row 1)
Tile 1: “Backup Freshness (Prod)”
- Value: % deployments with last_success_age <= 24h
- Secondary: list of outliers (last_success_age > 36h)
- Color: green >= 99%, yellow 95–99%, red < 95%

Tile 2: “Backup Success Rate (7d)”
- SLI definition: successful_backups / attempted_backups
- Successful = status=success AND integrity_check=pass
- Color: green >= 99.5%, yellow 99.0–99.5%, red < 99.0%

Tile 3: “Restore Drill Success (30d)”
- % of scheduled drills with status=success
- Note: staging drills are the default; prod drills optional per customer

Tile 4: “Restore Drill p95 Duration (30d)”
- End-to-end = restore_start -> validation_complete
- Show p50 + p95
- Overlay target line = RTO target for that archetype

Speaker notes:
We should not treat “backup succeeded” as true unless the artifact manifest and checksum verification pass.

—

Slide 6 — Mock: Backup success & attempts (time series)
Panel: “Backups — Attempts vs Successes (stacked)”
- X-axis: time (last 7d / 30d)
- Y-axis: count
- Series:
  - attempted_backups
  - successful_backups
  - failed_backups

Panel: “Backup Success Rate (rolling 6h / 24h)”
- Rolling windows to catch outages quickly
- Annotation markers: release deploys (installer version / chart version)

Panel: “Backup Job Duration (p50/p95)”
- Helps identify storage slowness (NFS) or throttling (S3)

Speaker notes:
Add deploy annotations because we’ve seen RBAC regressions and chart value changes break CronJobs. Being able to correlate is key.

—

Slide 7 — Mock: Backup freshness table (triage view)
Table: “Deployments with stale backups (last_success_age > 36h)”
Columns:
- deployment_id (link to deployment view)
- customer (if internal view; omit in customer-shared view)
- env
- deployment_type
- storage_backend
- last_success_ts
- last_attempt_ts
- last_error_category
- suggested_action

Suggested_action examples:
- “Check CronJob running + RBAC”
- “Verify S3 credentials/KMS policy”
- “NFS mount read-only / permission denied”
- “Clock skew detected; check node time sync”

Speaker notes:
This is the on-call panel. It should have “copy/paste commands” in the panel description (kubectl get jobs, installer backup status, etc.) but we keep those in the runbook link.

—

Slide 8 — Mock: Failure reasons (logs-to-metrics + top offenders)
Panel: “Backup Failures by Category (last 24h)”
Categories (initial set):
- RBAC_DENIED
- STORAGE_AUTH_FAILED
- KMS_UNAVAILABLE
- ENCRYPTION_ERROR
- SNAPSHOT_TIMEOUT
- INTEGRITY_CHECK_FAILED
- MISSING_CRDS
- UNKNOWN

Panel: “Top failing deployments (count, last 24h)”
- Click-through to logs/traces

Panel: “KMS latency / error rate (if available)”
- Separate visualization because customers often blame Redwood for KMS issues

Speaker notes:
We need consistency in error categories across installer + control-plane API + job logs. If categories drift, dashboards become useless.

—

Slide 9 — Mock: Artifact size and retention risk
Panel: “Backup Artifact Bytes (p50/p95)”
- Helps tune retention and detect runaway config DB growth

Panel: “Artifact Bytes by Backup Scope”
- control_plane vs audit_logs export vs k8s manifests

Panel: “Estimated storage consumption (retention * size)”
- Simple calc in dashboard description (not perfect)
- Warn when projected 30d retention exceeds X GB

Speaker notes:
This is partly for Solutions conversations (“why did my backup bucket grow?”). We should keep the math conservative and label as estimate.

—

Slide 10 — Mock: Restore drill overview
Panel: “Restore Drills — Success/Fail (last 30d)”
- Separate series for:
  - scheduled staging drills
  - optional customer prod drills

Panel: “Restore Drill Duration (end-to-end)”
- Show p50/p95; overlay target RTO line (dynamic by archetype)

Panel: “Validation failures by check”
Example checks:
- API health (control plane)
- Authn/authz sanity (admin login)
- Tenant config loaded (routing policy count matches)
- Model registry pointers resolve (references only)
- Audit log exporter checkpoint sanity

Speaker notes:
We should strongly differentiate “restore succeeded” vs “restore succeeded + validation passed”. On-call needs both.

—

Slide 11 — Alert thresholds (proposal)
Alert group A: Prod backup freshness (page)
- Condition: last_success_age > 36h for any prod deployment
- Severity: SEV2 page (customer impact risk)
- Suppress if maintenance_window=true label OR backup_suspended=true

Alert group B: Backup success rate drop (ticket / page depending)
- Condition: success_rate_24h < 99.0% AND attempted_backups_24h >= 10
- Severity: SEV3 ticket by default; SEV2 page if multiple prod deployments affected

Alert group C: Integrity check failures (page)
- Condition: integrity_check_failed > 0 in prod in last 6h
- Severity: SEV2 page (silent data corruption risk)

Alert group D: Restore drill failures (staging)
- Condition: last_scheduled_drill_status = fail
- Severity: Slack + ticket (no page outside business hours)

Alert group E: Restore drill RTO regression
- Condition: p95_restore_drill_duration > target_rto_minutes for 2 consecutive runs
- Severity: ticket; page if also correlated with prod incidents or release gate

Speaker notes:
This matches SRE guidance: page for prod backup freshness and integrity failures; don’t page engineers at 2am for staging drill flakiness.

—

Slide 12 — Noise controls & maintenance windows
Design knobs:
- Labels/flags:
  - maintenance_window=true
  - backup_suspended=true (explicit operator intent)
  - expected_failure=true (e.g., planned KMS migration)
- Alert routing:
  - staging drills: Slack #eng-sre + ticket
  - prod: on-call pager + #incidents (if widespread)
- Minimum sample sizes:
  - Don’t alert on success_rate until attempted_backups_24h >= N
- Burn-rate option (future):
  - If we adopt multi-window burn-rate for backup success SLO

Speaker notes:
We’ve previously had false positives when customers pause CronJobs during upgrades. We need a first-class “backup_suspended” mechanism in the toolkit so dashboards/alerts respect it.

—

Slide 13 — Customer-sharable vs internal views
Two dashboard modes (same base panels, different templating):
A) Customer-sharable
- No customer name list / no cross-deployment rollups
- Default filter pinned to deployment_id
- Links to public docs + customer runbooks

B) Internal (Redwood SRE)
- Rollups across deployments
- “Top failing deployments” table includes customer + account tier
- Links to internal Confluence runbooks + on-call notes

Speaker notes:
We want to minimize the number of dashboards we maintain, but we must avoid leaking cross-tenant info. Prefer folder-level ACL + templating.

—

Slide 14 — Implementation notes / dependencies (for ENG-9826/9827)
Assumed metrics (names are placeholders):
- redwood_private_backup_attempt_total{status}
- redwood_private_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds
- redwood_private_backup_duration_seconds
- redwood_private_backup_artifact_bytes
- redwood_private_backup_integrity_check_total{result}
- redwood_private_restore_drill_total{status}
- redwood_private_restore_drill_duration_seconds
- redwood_private_restore_validation_check_total{check,result}

Assumed logs/traces:
- trace spans around backup.create, restore.apply, validation.run
- error_category field standardized

Open questions:
- Where does maintenance_window label come from (Prometheus rule vs config in toolkit)?
- Do we surface KMS errors separately when KMS is customer-managed?
- Drill scheduling: weekly by default in staging, or daily until stable?

Speaker notes:
This slide is for the implementers. We should align on metric names ASAP to avoid rebuilding dashboards later.

—

Slide 15 — Next steps
- Review with SRE (Sean/Neha): alerting severities + paging policy
- Review with Private Deployments (Ethan/Vivek): ensure scope matches what we actually back up
- Add to observability-pack as a first iteration (behind “private_backup_restore” feature flag)
- Create a short “Dashboard tour” doc for Solutions + Support

Owner checklist:
[ ] Confirm SLO targets (backup success, drill latency) match RPO/RTO matrix
[ ] Ensure integrity verification is wired into the success definition
[ ] Add release annotations (installer + helm chart versions)
[ ] Decide on customer-facing language (avoid implying we back up K8s etcd)
